title: Universality of superdiffusion in simple random graphs
authors: Mrinal Sarkar, Nicolò Defenu, Tilman Enss
abstract: Random walks with long-range jumps can drive superdiffusive transport, replacing ordinary diffusion with an effective long-range kinetic operator. Such superdiffusive kinetics is also central to critical phenomena, notably the self-avoiding walk with long-range jump statistics, or Lévy-SAW. This work investigates how the critical behavior is affected when the long-range connectivity itself becomes random. We study self-avoiding walks (SAWs) on a one-dimensional long-range random ring graph, where bonds are independently generated with Bernoulli probability $\sim|i-j|^{-(1+σ)}$. We term this walk Sparse-SAW. The same random bonds are responsible for both long-range superdiffusive transport and quenched disorder, with both simultaneously controlled by the single parameter $σ$, placing the problem beyond the conventional Harris and Weinrib-Halperin frameworks. Through large-scale Monte Carlo simulations and a Gaussian-truncated field theory, we show that Sparse-SAW belongs to the same universality class as the clean superdiffusive Lévy-SAW. The random bonds generate short-range uncorrelated and long-range correlated mass disorder while simultaneously producing the long-range kinetic operator. Under coarse-graining, the latter dominates, restoring the clean critical behavior. Our study suggests that the full non-Gaussian Bernoulli statistics may lead to disorder physics beyond the conventional theory of quenched disorder, while establishing random graphs as an efficient platform for extracting the critical exponents of the clean superdiffusive Lévy-SAW universality class.
summary: This work analyzes self-avoiding walks on random graphs whose connectivity induces superdiffusive transport. By using field theory and Monte Carlo simulations, the authors demonstrate that the random graph disorder is irrelevant at criticality. This establishes random graphs as a useful platform for confirming the critical exponents of the clean superdiffusive Lévy-SAW universality class.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the critical behavior of self-avoiding walks (SAWs) is affected when the underlying connectivity of the graph itself is random, particularly when this randomness controls both superdiffusive transport and quenched disorder.
main_result: The critical exponents of the Sparse-SAW on a random graph agree with those of the clean superdiffusive Lévy-SAW, suggesting that the random graph belongs to the same universality class.
method: The study employs large-scale Monte Carlo simulations and develops a Gaussian-truncated field theory approach, utilizing the replica trick to average over the random graph disorder.
model_or_system: The system models SAWs on a one-dimensional long-range random ring graph, where bonds are generated with a probability decaying as $|i-j|^{-(1+\sigma)}$. This setup allows the single parameter $\sigma$ to control both the long-range superdiffusive kinetic operator and the quenched disorder.
key_observables:
Critical exponents ($
u_{LR}$ and $\gamma$) characterizing the SAW behavior, and the asymptotic decay of the propagator $G(x) \sim |x|^{-1-\sigma}$.
important_parameters: The decay exponent $\sigma$ of the random bond probability, which controls the crossover between short-range and long-range physics.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the replica trick for disorder averaging and assumes that under coarse-graining, the long-range kinetic operator dominates the disorder effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the calculated critical exponents for Lévy-SAW and Sparse-SAW as a function of $\sigma$, showing agreement with the clean Flory prediction in the long-range regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical system (SAWs on random graphs) and the associated disorder/transport mechanism. It then applies field theory and replica methods to calculate the disorder-averaged action and propagator, ultimately comparing the resulting critical exponents to the clean system predictions.
why_interesting: The finding that correlated graph disorder is irrelevant at criticality, leaving the clean critical behavior intact, provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding how disorder affects critical phenomena in systems with long-range interactions.
